questions.text:
An organization requires a range of IP address to assign one to each of its 1500 computers. The organization has approached an Internet Service Provider (ISP) for this task. The ISP uses CIDR and serves the requests from the available IP address space 202.61.0.0/17. The ISP wants to assign an address space to the organization which will minimize the number of routing entries in the ISP?s router using route aggregation. Which of the following address spaces are potential candidates from which the ISP can allot any one of the organization?

I. 202.61.84.0/21
II. 202.61.104.0/21
III. 202.61.64.0/21
IV. 202.61.144.0/21
questions.solution:
1500 hosts need [latex]2^{11}=2048[/latex] addresses [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a /21 block. A /21 must start at a third octet that is a multiple of 8, and lie inside 202.61.0.0/17 (third octet 0-127).

- I: 84 is not a multiple of 8 False
- II: 104 = 13 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 True
- III: 64 = 8 [latex]\times[/latex] 8 True
- IV: 144 is outside the /17 range False

Answer: II and III only

questions.text: Assume that you have made a request for a web page through your web browser to a web server. Initially the browser cache is empty. Further, the browser is configured to send HTTP requests in non-persistent mode. The web page contains text and five very small images.The minimum number of TCP connections required to display the web page completely in your browser is__________.
questions.solution:
Non-persistent HTTP uses a separate TCP connection for each object: 1 for the HTML page + 5 for the images.

Answer: 6

questions.text:
Consider the following statements about the functionality of an IP based router.

I. A router does not modify the IP packets during forwarding.
II. It is not necessary for a router to implement any routing protocol.
III. A router should reassemble IP fragments if the MTU of the outgoing link is larger than the size of the incoming IP packet.

Which of the above statements is/are TRUE?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- I: a router changes the packet (TTL decrement, checksum, possibly fragmentation) [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- II: a router can work with static routes only, without any routing protocol [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- III: routers never reassemble fragments; only the destination does [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.

Answer: II only

questions.text: In an RSA cryptosystem, the value of the public modulus parameter n is 3007. If it is also is known that [latex]\phi(n)=2880[/latex], where [latex]\phi()[/latex] denotes Euler's Totient Function, then the prime factors of n which is greater than 50 is _________ .
questions.solution:
n = pq and [latex]\phi(n)=(p-1)(q-1)=n-(p+q)+1[/latex].
So [latex]p+q=3007-2880+1=128[/latex] and [latex]pq=3007[/latex].

p, q are roots of [latex]t^2-128t+3007=0[/latex]: [latex]t=\frac{128\pm\sqrt{16384-12028}}{2}=\frac{128\pm66}{2}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 97 and 31.

Answer: 97

questions.text: Consider that 15 machines need to be connected in a LAN using 8-port Ethernet switches. Assume that these switches do not have any separate up link ports. The minimum number of switches needed is ___________.
questions.solution:
Connecting switches uses ports (one port on each side of each link).
- 2 switches: 16 ports [latex]-[/latex] 2 for the link = 14 [latex]\lt[/latex] 15 False
- 3 switches in a chain: 24 ports [latex]-[/latex] 4 for 2 links = 20 [latex]\ge[/latex] 15 True

Answer: 3
